$comment: GitGit required status-check contexts — the JOB NAMES that the branch protection is expected to require. GitHub reports a check under a job's `name:`, so these strings are the context strings: changing one of them here without changing the protection leaves the protection requiring a check that is never reported, which is the same deadlock as a path-filtered workflow, one string away. The names below are the EXISTING job names, character for character, which is why adding them to the branch protection cannot silently miss. The deep-gate refactor (docs/plan/deep-gate-enforcement.md) moved the path filter from the workflow level into the jobs in ALL FIVE workflows, so these jobs now report on EVERY pull request — a job skipped by its own `if:` condition is reported as 'Success', which satisfies a required check, whereas a workflow that never starts reports nothing and leaves the check Pending forever. FULLY ENFORCED as of 2026-10-25 23:20 JST: the branch protection on `dev` and `main` requires `repo gate (always runs)` plus ALL FOURTEEN contexts below. The five of rust-backend.yml, gm-console.yml and frontend-audit.yml were measured on PR #60 and PR #61; the nine of gm-desktop.yml and gm-desktop-bundle.yml on PR #62, and the whole set was then observed reporting on a pull request that touched none of the five areas (PR #63), where the three consumer jobs were SKIPPED as a whole and their three producers reported green without doing the work. The notes below say which is which, so this file never claims more than is true.

notes.enforcementNote: [FACT] The GitHub branch protection DOES now require more than the one always-running gate. `dev` and `main` require `repo gate (always runs)` plus ALL FOURTEEN contexts below — the five of rust-backend.yml, gm-console.yml and frontend-audit.yml, and the nine of gm-desktop.yml and gm-desktop-bundle.yml. The protection was changed with the narrow endpoint (PATCH .../protection/required_status_checks), so every other setting was read before and after and is unchanged: strict, enforce_admins, linear history, the review count, conversation resolution, and the deletion and force-push bans. [FACT] The five were measured on PR #60 and PR #61: a pull request that touches none of the frontend files still reported `frontend dependency advisories (npm ratchet)`, in 15 seconds, where before the change the workflow would not have started at all and the check would have stayed Pending for ever. [FACT] The nine were measured on PR #62, where every one of them ran and passed, and they are required as of 2026-10-25. [FACT] The verification that is still owed: a pull request that touches NONE of the five areas must make all fourteen report green rather than Pending, and the three consumer jobs (`msi installs and removes itself on a stock Windows machine`, `the packaged application starts and presents a window`, `deb installs and links on a stock Ubuntu`) must be SKIPPED as a whole rather than run and fail on an artefact that was never uploaded. That is the one behaviour in this arrangement that has not yet been observed on a pull request.
notes.laneScope: [FACT] These fourteen contexts are the job names of all five gated areas. Lane L1-a owns the three rust-backend.yml jobs, the one gm-console.yml job and the one frontend-audit.yml job — the five that were required first, on 2026-10-25 22:35 JST. Lane L1-b owns the three gm-desktop.yml jobs and the four gm-desktop-bundle.yml jobs — the nine that were required afterwards, on 2026-10-25 23:20 JST. [FACT] All five workflows have now moved their path filter out of the workflow and into the jobs, so every one of these fourteen jobs reports on EVERY pull request. [FACT] Five of the release.yml jobs used to carry the same display names as their pull-request counterparts; the release side now carries a `release ` prefix, so each of the fourteen names below is the name of exactly ONE job across every workflow file — which is what apps/gm-desktop/tests/unit/workflow-gate.test.ts asserts.
notes.verification: [UNVERIFIED-FACT] GitHub's path-matching component is not open source, so the local equivalence between scripts/ci/changed-areas.ps1 and GitHub's own `paths:` semantics is an inference, not a fact. The real verification is the empirical pull-request check. [UNVERIFIED-FACT] YAML that parses is not YAML GitHub accepts: the workflow parser is GitHub's own, so it is verified by a pull request and not by a test. [FACT] One more GitHub behaviour was measured and found not to be what a design assumed: a job whose steps are ALL skipped does not become skipped — it concludes SUCCESS — and a dependency that succeeds does not skip its dependents. The consumer jobs therefore take the producer's area decision as an output and carry a job-level `if:`, because a consumer that inferred the decision from the producer's success would run and fail on an artefact that was never uploaded.
